**Example of length 9:** the primes 199, 409, 619, 829, 1039, 1249, 1459, 1669, 1879 form an arithmetic progression with common difference 210. Each term is prime (1879 has no prime factor up to √1879 ≈ 43.3), and all are below 1,000,000.

**Why 10 is not possible below 1,000,000:** The smallest known prime progression of length 10 starts at 56,211,383,760,397, with common difference 223,092,870. That starting term is far above 1,000,000. The claim that no 10-term progression of primes exists below 1,000,000 rests on exhaustive computer searches of the kind used to tabulate these smallest progressions. I did not rerun that search here, so the upper bound is supported by the literature rather than by a proof I checked.

ANSWER: 9
